title: Inventor to Revit Export Instructions
purpose: Execute the governed Inventor-to-Revit export workflow with a BIM-appropriate representation, validated artifact behavior, and auditable export metadata.
preconditions: The Inventor source model opens successfully.

steps.name: Confirm export intent
steps.purpose: Select the correct Revit artifact type from intended use.
actions: Confirm whether the artifact is for project/coordination representation or reusable component use.
Record export intent as RVT or RFA.

steps.name: Prepare BIM-appropriate representation
steps.purpose: Prevent unnecessary manufacturing detail from degrading downstream BIM use.
actions: Suppress unnecessary fasteners and internal features.
Confirm only geometry relevant to the declared downstream use remains.
validation: Representation is visually simplified for the declared BIM use.

steps.name: Select export-specific Model State
steps.purpose: Provide a repeatable representation for subsequent exports.
actions: Create or select the Model State intended for Revit export.
Use an approved export-specific naming convention; source examples include Revit_Light and Revit_Medium.

steps.name: Configure RVT export settings
steps.purpose: Create the governed Revit project representation when the RVT path applies.
actions: Open the RVT export workflow.
Set Preset to No Simplification because simplification has been handled in the approved Inventor representation.
Select the approved Model State.
Select the approved export View.
Set output structure to Each top-level component.
Enable updating when the governed update path is required.
validation: Settings match the approved export checklist and project/tool-version constraints.
failure_modes: Updating omitted where the governed update path requires it.

steps.name: Configure RFA export settings
steps.purpose: Create a reusable Revit Family component when the RFA path applies.
actions: Assign the correct Revit category.
Add connectors only when required by the intended component behavior.
Confirm expected family behavior and downstream use.
validation: Category and behavior match the declared use.
failure_modes: Behavior does not match intended use.

steps.name: Execute export
actions: Run the configured export.
Allow the export to complete without interruption.
Save the artifact to the governed working location.

steps.name: Validate export in Revit
actions: Open or load the exported artifact in Revit.
Check orientation, scale, and geometry.
Check performance and file size against the declared use.
Check expected category or behavior for RFA artifacts.
validation: Artifact opens or loads cleanly and behaves as expected for the declared use.

steps.name: Verify update workflow
steps.purpose: Confirm controlled source changes can be propagated where updating is part of the selected path.
preconditions: Updating is enabled and required for the selected RVT workflow.
actions: Make or use a controlled source change.
Update or re-export according to the supported Inventor workflow.
Confirm target Revit behavior and retained dependencies where applicable.
validation: Update behavior is verified without uncontrolled authority or dependency changes.

steps.name: Record export metadata
actions: Record date, source/version context, Model State or representation, export type, settings, and validation result.
Attach or register the record in the applicable coordination or exchange log.
validation: Export metadata record exists and identifies the source and exported artifact.

evidence: Successful Revit open/load or component load
governance_notes: The source names Revit_Light and Revit_Medium as examples, not as a closed canonical vocabulary.
Current Autodesk documentation confirms RVT simplification/export and updating capabilities but tool-version behavior remains implementation evidence rather than normative authority.
Technical export success does not equal project acceptance or formal exchange.

provenance.migration_note: Migrated all nine source instructions. Examples were preserved as examples; project acceptance and current tool-version capability remain separate governance/evidence concerns.
